what_it_does: When engineers design a chip, they write a blueprint called RTL (Register-Transfer Level description) that specifies exactly how data moves through logic gates. A common logic element in those blueprints is a multiplexer — essentially a digital selector switch that routes one of several inputs to an output. After synthesis (the automated step that turns the blueprint into actual gate-level hardware), large trees of redundant multiplexers can remain, wasting chip area and power. SmaRTLy is an optimization tool that analyzes the logical relationships between signals in the design to detect multiplexer trees whose outputs can never differ — making them redundant — and removes them. It then rebuilds the remaining multiplexers into more compact structures. The key advance over existing tools is that SmaRTLy looks beyond individual multiplexers to understand how signals relate to each other globally, catching redundancies that simpler, local analyses miss.
